newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs, Norway finalise 20-year gas supply deal.
newsitem.headline: Czechs, Norway finalise 20-year gas supply deal.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy on Wednesday said a 20-year, 53 billion cubic metre (bcm) deal to supply Norwegian natural gas has been finalised.
"I am pleased and honoured to say...that the final negotiations were completed," Dlouhy told a business forum with representatives of the Norwegian government and Norway's King Harald.
Dlouhy said supplies of the gas should begin on May 1, 1997, and gradually grow to 3 bcm per year.
The deal is expected to be presented to the government in the coming weeks, which must first approve it before state-owned gas transporter Transgas will sign the final contract.
The agreement signals an end to more than 50 years of total dependence on Russia.

Although Prague's political domination by Moscow ended with its 1989 democratic revolution, the Czechs have still relied on Russia for most of its energy needs and Russian raw materials will remain a major element of Czech imports.

Dlouhy said on Tuesday that Czech moves to build a pipeline linking Prague to Middle Eastern oil from the Adriatic Sea, to buy U.S. supplied nuclear fuel for Czech power plants, and the Norway gas deal, completed "our strategic long-term targets".
The ministry was considering other options including potential deals with German, Dutch and British suppliers or a second delivery route of Russian gas.

Czechs consume around nine bcms per year of natural gas, with demand expecting to rise to 12 to 13 bcms after the turn of the century. Russia's Gazprom is still expected to remain a main supplier to the Czechs.

The deal, on the eve of a summit between U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin where Czech NATO membership is to be discussed, also comes soon after Russia's ambassador to Prague hinted of economic reprisals should the Czechs join the western security alliance.
